key_insight: Forked PINNs add a dedicated control branch with selective gradient flow, letting simulation and control be trained jointly in non-Markovian open quantum systems without the usual optimization conflict.
engineering_relevance: This provides a unified, differentiable workflow for quantum state preparation and open-system control, with smoother pulses and better robustness than common baselines.
method: Extend FPINN with a separate control branch for open quantum dynamics.
Use selective gradient flow to decouple competing objectives at the gradient level.
Jointly optimize simulation and control on the same physics-informed model.
evidence_signal: On a two-qubit Heisenberg XXX model, the method reproduced non-Markovian effects such as decoherence and information backflow and achieved higher state-preparation fidelity than GAPE, CRAB, and standard PINNs.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful training design, since standard PINNs are reported to struggle with convergence in coupled non-Markovian objectives.
paper_title: Forked Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Non-Markovian Open Quantum Dynamics and Control
